Based on my review, this diff adds a new `field_validator` on `InstanceConfig.url` that wires the already-existing `validate_arr_url_config` (added in a prior commit, unchanged here) into Pydantic model construction. This closes a real gap: previously, URLs loaded directly from `triggarr.toml` (as opposed to URLs submitted through the web settings form, which already went through the strict `validate_arr_url` at `triggarr/web/routes.py:561`) had no SSRF validation at all. This is a tightening change on the SSRF axis — it adds a new blocklist check where none existed before — so per the review calibration rules it's presumptively safe and I looked for a concrete bypass rather than assuming one.

Findings:
- No bypass of the new check's own changed lines: the relaxed variant still blocks link-local/unspecified/multicast IP literals, cloud-metadata hosts/IPs, and non-http(s) schemes; it deliberately permits loopback/`localhost` by design (D-02, "legitimate homelab pattern"), which is a documented, tested product decision, not an SSRF hole.
- Any residual DNS-rebinding / hostname-based bypass (non-IP-literal hostnames aren't resolved at validation time) lives entirely in the pre-existing, unchanged `validate_arr_url_config`/`validate_arr_url` helper logic in `triggarr/web/validation.py` (not part of this diff) and is already explicitly called out in that code's own docstring as an accepted residual risk shared by every existing caller (including the web-form path). Per the pre-existing-gap rule this doesn't lift the cap for this diff.
- I checked the one call site that builds `InstanceConfig` from untrusted web input (`save_settings` in `triggarr/web/routes.py:551-601`) and confirmed it already runs the *stricter* `validate_arr_url` before model construction, so the new, more permissive config-load validator never weakens that path — it only adds coverage for direct TOML edits.
- A behavioral side effect I considered but did not file as a security finding: because `pydantic.ValidationError` is allowed to propagate uncaught from `ensure_config()` (per `triggarr/config.py`'s own docstring), a pre-existing deployment with a disabled instance's URL that now trips this validator (e.g., a stray link-local or malformed URL) would crash at startup with an uncaught traceback rather than a friendly error. agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig in triggarr/models/config.py is imported by about 9 runtime modules and more than 16 test files. The public API is unchanged: no field or signature changes, and validation only rejects more inputs. Startup path: per triggarr/config.py:345, ValidationError from ensure_config propagates uncaught. So any rejected URL, including on a disabled instance (an intended choice per the docstring), means a traceback and exit at boot. That is the main user-facing risk of this diff (see impact-1).

findings.title: Load-time and UI-save validators disagree on loopback IPs: config with 127.0.0.1 loads but any settings save is silently refused
findings.why_it_matters: Same-host users, whom D-02 explicitly supports, cannot save any settings through the UI.

agent_notes: Checked diff (triggarr/models/config.py, new validate_url_ssrf field_validator on InstanceConfig.url) against root CLAUDE.md security rules (no SQLi/subprocess/innerHTML/hardcoded secrets/sensitive logging) and correctness rules (nullable guards, resource release, floating promises, silent exception swallowing) — none apply; the validator raises ValueError (propagates, not swallowed) and touches no secrets, I/O, or external calls.

Checked against project CLAUDE.md Code Conventions (ruff E/F/I/UP/B/SIM, line length 120, SecretStr discipline, Loguru-only logging, atomic writes, pytest-asyncio) — url is a plain str field (SecretStr rule doesn't apply to it), no logging/print statements added, no file writes, added lines are well under 120 chars.

Verified the local `from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config` import (inside the function body rather than module top) follows an existing repo precedent for breaking cross-module import direction: triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532/538 does the same local-import pattern for `triggarr.web.routes` imports. triggarr/web/__init__.py and triggarr/models/__init__.py are both empty, so no actual circular-import exists either way, but the new code matches the established style for this situation per the global CLAUDE.md instruction to follow existing conventions before introducing a new pattern.

Confirmed this is tracked, intentional, tested work: commit 14eecb5 ('feat(71-02): add validate_arr_url_config() relaxed SSRF validator') added the sibling function in triggarr/web/validation.py, and tests/test_config.py already has a D-01/D-02/D-03 test block (lines ~290-336) exercising InstanceConfig's config-load SSRF validation, loopback/localhost acceptance, and ordering relative to reject_apikey_in_url.
Deep Code Review Convention item 5 ('Pydantic validation before any config write') is satisfied by construction — the validator runs at field-validation time, before any config write path.
No rule violations found.

Local import of validate_arr_url_config inside validate_url_ssrf (triggarr/models/config.py:106) was checked for a circular-import rationale: triggarr/web/validation.py has no dependency back on triggarr.models, so a module-level import would also work — the local import appears to be a defensive/narrow-coupling choice rather than a necessity. Not flagged as a defect; it executes once per InstanceConfig validation (config load / settings POST), not in a hot loop, so there's no meaningful perf cost.

No mutable-default, bare-except, is-vs-eq, missing-type-hint, or unreleased-resource issues found in the added validator — it's a pure string-in/string-out field_validator consistent with the sibling reject_apikey_in_url validator's style and type-hint conventions already established in this file.

Pydantic v2 default field_validator mode is 'after'; multiple after-validators on the same field run in class-body declaration order, so reject_apikey_in_url (apikey check) executes before validate_url_ssrf (SSRF check) here — confirmed consistent with the docstrings' stated intent, no ordering bug.
No substantive defect found in the added validator. Existing controls remain intact. Targeted checks: 60 passed; two filesystem-dependent tests were blocked by the read-only sandbox.
